author: Zack Priehs
title: 'We want transparency': Mother on daughter's East Lansing arrest - NewsBreak
text:
By Zack Priehs ,
16 minutes ago
EAST LANSING, Mich. (WLNS) — A mother is speaking out against the East Lansing Police Department after watching video of her daughter being tased, handcuffed and punched by officers during an arrest over the weekend.
Video surfaced on social media on Sunday depicting 20-year-old Myana Collins being detained outside Harpers Restaurant and Brew Pub in downtown East Lansing, one multiple people and organizations like the NAACP Lansing Branch say is just another example of ELPD officers using excessive force against a Black person.
Myana Collins’ family, including her father (left), younger sister (middle) and mother, Shannon (right). (WLNS) 6 News obtained an exclusive interview with Collins’ mother, Shannon, who spoke with us on the condition we do not publish her last name.
She shared how Sunday’s incident has affected her and her daughter and also spoke in front of the East Lansing Independent Police Oversight Commission Wednesday, with Police Chief Jen Brown in attendance.
“We’ve all painfully watched the video footage, we’ve watched Myana handcuffed and restrained by multiple officers,” Shannon told the officers.
Shannon has spent the last couple of days processing what happened to her daughter on Sunday. She told 6 News she’s aware of other questionable East Lansing policing incidents, like last August’s pepper spraying of 2 young Black men, and the officer-involved shooting death of of Michigan State University student Isaiah Kirby.
But she never thought it would happen to her own child.
“I mean we knew it was possible because we’ve seen this happen to other people’s children, but you never thing it’s gonna happen to your own child. But then it did,” Shannon added.
ELPD has confirmed it is investigating the incident, and has placed one officer on paid leave. They’re also investigating what happened at the East Lansing Jail, where Shannon said medical records show her daughter fell, hit her head and later received a CT scan at the hospital.
Video from Sunday’s incident appears to show Collins being struck multiple times in the back by an officer, something Shannon says was both traumatizing and physically harmful.
“I mean she’s traumatized. She’s, y’know, trying to heal but she’s just very traumatized. she’s trying to heal physically and mentally,” Shannon added.
6 News also spoke to James McCurtis, the president of the Lansing NAACP Branch. He renewed his call for Police Chief Jen Brown to resign, or be fired and described Sunday’s incident as “inexcusable.”
“My first reaction was outrage, and then for a police officer to haul off and punch her several times,” said McCurtis “There was no excuse for that, inexcusable.”
Meanwhile, Shannon wants answers. She says the name of the game is transparency.
“We don’t know why that they approached her. We have a lot of questions,” she said. “That’s why we want answers. We want the body cam footage, we want transparency from the department.”
Shannon said she seconds the calls for Brown to resign, adding that she’s afraid for her daughter’s safety while in East Lansing. She tells 6 News she has been able to see her daughter since Sunday, and says it’s been a lot of hugs, and reminding Collins that she’s there to support.
